Today's Easy Decluttering Project - Sheets

DAY SIX of looking at this series and hopefully making it easy for both of us to follow.

Oh sheet! Yes the linen closet, hmmm, it’s time.

Truth be told we can only use one set of sheets on the bed(s) at a time, so one extra set for laundry days is allowed but anything more and your linen will be jumping out to greet you everytime you open the door, aka clutter.

There are some neat videos on how to fold the fitted sheet, flat sheet into the pillowcases to make one bundle. This is great for no mess, no fuss and easy access. Think about how to make your life easier this is what this series is all about.

We know that each bed can only use one set of sheets at a time.

{Note: if you have bed-wetters in your house, you get a free pass to keep a few extra sets of sheets. Ain't nobody got the time to be doing that much laundry on a daily basis!} <- try keeping these extra sets in the actual room if possible as these things often happen in the middle of the night and looking for linen becomes a horrible task half asleep while tearing your linen closet apart trying to find a suitable replacement, {Geez, if only I knew this when I had my first child, oh well we live and we learn!}

Let’s check how to to sort this out!

Normally I'd start with throwing out any garbage, but with sheets, you can always use torn sheets as rags or donate them to an animal shelter. So unless you've got some other kinds of garbage that have found their way into your sheet piles, let's move on to donating and giving away.

  • Donate or give away any worn out or torn sheets

  • Donate or give away any sets that are missing parts {unless you're going for the mismatched look}

  • Donate or give away any sheets that you have not used in the last 3 months {except for any seasonal sheets - like extra warm flannel sheets for winter}

  • Donate or give away any sized sheets that you don't own beds for {e.g. crib/toddler size sheets when your kids have moved into twin sized beds, full size sheets for a pull-out couch you no longer own, etc.}

  • Of the sheets you have left, choose the 2 sets you love the most, for each bed in your home, and then give away all the rest.

I also find quilts and blankets hard to store but there are vacuum sealed bags that reduce the bulk of it and I store these out of the way, out of season.

  • If you can use linen to make rag rugs, remove and store elsewhere. Donating sheets right now to VBS is a good idea as they use it for decor and Biblical attire etc.

Happy linen day ladies!
